definition.title: retryWithBackoff Call Audit
definition.problemStatement:
Collaborate on the requested project task.
User idea: I need answers about this codebase, not changes to it. Find out which files under src/ call retryWithBackoff, what number of attempts it uses by default, and which callers override the number of attempts and with what value.
Write what you find to FINDINGS.md. End the file with one fenced json block of exactly this shape, with paths relative to the repository root:
{"callers": ["src/a.js"], "defaultAttempts": 3, "attemptOverrides": {"src/a.js": 2}}
Do not change any source file. Research this as a team: start a research Room of two agents who each test a different reading of the code and check each other's findings, and do not do the research yourself.
Question: In the repository at the project root (read-only), determine exactly: (1) the set of file paths under src/ that call retryWithBackoff, given as paths relative to the repository root; (2) the default number of attempts retryWithBackoff uses when its attempts option is not supplied, as read from its implementation (and re-exported wrappers, if any); (3) which of those callers pass an explicit attempt/retries count instead of relying on the default, and the exact numeric value each passes. Also note any callers that reach retryWithBackoff indirectly (through a wrapper, alias, or dynamic property access) so the caller list is complete and not just literal-name matches.
Stop when: Stop when both members have separately produced the caller list, the default attempt count and the override map from the code, and each has re-verified the other's claims against the cited file lines; every disagreement is resolved by re-reading the cited lines and the final answer states the resolved values with file:line citations. Do not modify any source file.
Work together to investigate the question, challenge assumptions and produce concrete findings with evidence and unresolved user decisions. Do not implement the product.

blueprint.title: retryWithBackoff Call Audit
blueprint.approach: Two researchers independently trace direct and indirect call paths, exchange only concrete claims and citations for cross-verification, then consolidate the verified findings into the requested report.
blueprint.objective: Determine every src/ caller of retryWithBackoff, its implementation default attempts value, all explicit caller overrides, and document the verified evidence in FINDINGS.md.
successCriteria: FINDINGS.md identifies all direct and indirect callers under src/ with repository-relative paths and file:line citations.
The default attempts value is traced to the implementation and any relevant wrapper or re-export path.
Every explicit attempts or retries override is mapped to its exact numeric value.
The report ends with one fenced JSON block matching the requested shape exactly.
blueprint.roomInstructions: Research the repository rather than changing source code. Search broadly for imports, aliases, wrappers, re-exports, property access, and call expressions; cite the lines supporting every conclusion. Produce independent initial results before exchanging concise claims for verification. Resolve disagreements by reopening cited code, and keep the report’s final JSON block exact.

members.responsibility: Trace call sites and consolidate mutually verified evidence into FINDINGS.md.
members.mandate: Independently audit src/ for direct call expressions, imports, aliases, and call-site options, producing a cited initial caller and override inventory. Coordinate the shared brief, request the other researcher’s independent implementation and indirection findings, and send concise claims rather than reasoning for cross-checking. Re-read every cited claim received, resolve discrepancies through source evidence, and write FINDINGS.md with human-readable cited conclusions followed by the exact requested fenced JSON block. Do not modify source files, do not substitute unsupported guesses for evidence, and do not take over the other researcher’s implementation/wrapper analysis. Report the final resolved inventory and any genuinely unresolved ambiguity to the Room.
promptAdditions: Treat completeness as an audit requirement: search naming variants and trace local aliases before concluding a caller list is exhaustive.
Place file:line citations in the narrative findings before the final JSON block.
members.reasonForInclusion: Without a coordinator who also audits call sites, there would be no accountable consolidation of cross-verified evidence into the required findings file.

members.responsibility: Independently trace retryWithBackoff’s implementation, wrappers, and indirect callers, then verify the Conductor’s claims.
members.mandate: Independently locate retryWithBackoff’s defining implementation, exports and re-exports, and trace wrapper, alias, and dynamic-property routes to callers under src/. Determine the default attempt behavior and every explicit numeric override with file:line citations, and send an initial evidence inventory to the Conductor without adopting the Conductor’s reasoning. After receiving concise claims and citations from the Conductor, independently re-open the cited lines and report confirmations or discrepancies with corrected evidence. Do not edit files, do not prepare FINDINGS.md, do not redo the Conductor’s call-site assignment beyond verification, and refer unresolved interpretation questions to the Conductor.
promptAdditions: Start from implementation and exports, not from literal call-name search results.
Distinguish an explicit retry count from unrelated numeric options and cite the exact syntax that establishes the value.
members.reasonForInclusion: Without an independent implementation and indirection audit, wrapper-mediated callers and the actual default value could be missed or accepted without independent verification.

blueprint.teamRationale: This pair combines a call-site-focused audit with an implementation-and-indirection-focused audit, so literal matches and less obvious routes receive separate scrutiny before consolidation.
blueprint.collaborationStrategy: The Conductor assigns distinct investigation lenses and collects each researcher’s initial evidence without sharing reasoning. They then exchange caller, default, and override claims with citations, independently inspect the cited lines, report resolutions to the Conductor, and the Conductor prepares the final findings document.
openAssumptions: FINDINGS.md does not already contain required material that must be preserved.
A caller is a source file that invokes retryWithBackoff either directly or through a statically traceable local wrapper, alias, or property path.
